articles: Learning JavaScript from scratch: where to start?
A sensible learning order for beginners, without jumping straight into frameworks.
Programming
Many people give up on JavaScript because they jump straight into a framework. The basics can be learned in a few weeks.
## Master the basics first
Learn variables, functions, arrays, and objects. Build small programs like a calculator or a shopping list in the browser.
## Frameworks come after
Once you're comfortable with the basics and the DOM, frameworks like React will make much more sense.
Five simple habits to keep your online accounts safe
Small steps that prevent most account takeovers.
Security
Most accounts get broken into not by genius hackers, but because of reused passwords.
## Use a password manager
One strong password for the manager, then let it create a unique password for every account.
## Turn on two-step verification
Enable it on your email and social media. The extra code means a leaked password isn't enough to get in.
How to care for your laptop so it lasts
Daily habits that keep your laptop fast and cool.
Devices
A slow laptop often isn't broken, just neglected.
## Keep the air flowing
Don't use your laptop on the bed. Clean the dust from the vents every few months.
## Trim startup apps
Turn off apps that don't need to run when the laptop starts.
Git for beginners: saving your code's history
Commits, branches, and pushes explained with simple examples.
Programming
Git saves the history of your code changes, like an undo button that can rewind time.
## A commit is a save point
Each commit saves the state of your code along with a short note.
## Branches for trying new things
Create a branch before trying a new feature, so your main code stays safe.
Choosing a phone for work and school
The specs that really matter, and the ones you can ignore.
Reviews
A big camera number doesn't always mean a phone that's right for work.
## Prioritize RAM and battery
For running many apps at once, RAM and battery life make the biggest difference.
## Check the update support window
A phone that gets regular security updates stays safer for years.
